newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hebron deal with Israel close, Palestinians say.
newsitem.headline: Hebron deal with Israel close, Palestinians say.

text.p: Israeli and Palestinian negotiators are close to agreement on the long-delayed Israeli troop pull-back from the West Bank town of Hebron, Palestinian officials said on Thursday.
"There might be some problems in the drafting but the issues have been resolved," said one official, who declined to be identified.

"If there are no problems in the drafting, within 24 hours there will be positive results and an agreement. The only remaining issue is the drafting of the protocol which explains the steps of implementing the Hebron redeployment," he said.

Israeli and Palestinian negotiators were meeting long into the night in Eilat in Israel and Taba in Egypt, neighbouring Red Sea resorts, to hammer out an agreement on the long-delayed pullback from Hebron.

U.S. envoy Dennis Ross was helping them draft a protocol for implementing the deal. Palestinian officials said it could be signed on Friday or Sunday, possibly in Taba, and would start coming into force 10 days later.

Israel has held up redeployment of its troops, citing security concerns for the 400 Jews who live and study in enclaves among 100,000 Arabs. The city is sacred to Moslems and Jews as the burial place of the biblical Abraham.

Israeli spokesman Moshe Fogel declined comment, except to say that talks were continuing on both sides. "We are at the point where both sides are trying to identify points of mutual understanding," he said.

The Palestinian official said major stumbling blocks were removed during a meeting on Thursday between Israeli army chief Amnon Shahak, PLO negotiator Abu Mazen, Palestinian Information Minister Yasser Abed Rabbu and Ross.
Palestinian officials said Israel was no longer insisting on establishing a buffer zone or on the right to hot pursuit of wanted Palestinians in areas coming under PLO control.
In tension-packed Hebron itself on Thursday, Israeli police pulled down a fence that Jewish settlers had begun erecting around an Arab-owned hilltop.

The settlers hammered spikes around the sparsely planted hilltop and began extending barbed wire, sparking a row with Palestinian landowners, witnesses said. Police separated the two sides and ordered the settlers to halt the work.
A Palestinian official said it was also agreed that talks on all other outstanding issues in a 1995 interim deal would start immediately after the Hebron agreement was concluded.

These issues would include further redeployments, the release of Palestinian prisoners, safe passage between the West Bank and Gaza Strip, operation of a Gaza airport for Palestinians and allowing more Palestinians to work in Israel.
